# *Aeden Thomas*, Software Engineer

I had the pleasure of working closely alongside Stephen at Shoutt, where he served as our Lead Data Scientist. He was the first data scientist I collaborated with, and he set an exceptionally high standard for what cross-functional partnership between engineering and data science should look like. Data science and applied AI often demand weeks or months of deep, painstaking iteration, and Stephen’s patience in this area is extraordinary. He is a true expert at diving into complex, ambiguous data, diagnosing edge cases, and methodically driving up accuracy through disciplined evaluation loops. Just as impressive was his approach to problem-solving and the sheer clarity of his documentation. Whether he was engineering prompt and evaluation frameworks or building out our dashboards to give the team visibility into user funnels, Stephen always documented his reasoning, test suites, and trade-offs meticulously. He took the mystery out of the AI layer and made complex systems easy for the engineering team to understand and build upon. Stephen is a fantastic data scientist, a patient and clear-headed thinker, and an outstanding teammate. Any team would be lucky to have him, and I recommend him without hesitation.

# *Jonathan Eadie*, Co-founder, Shoutt

I worked very closely with Stephen at Shoutt. Stephen is a very talented Lead Data Scientist. He owned several large projects including classifying the role type for thousands of inconsistent job posts into clean, reliable data that we could match to users. He also lead the AI on our CV review tool where he engineered a substantial prompt framework and an evaluation framework. Throughout he worked with a freelance tester to produce a high quality chat bot type tool that helped users improve their CV. His work on the evaluation pipelines has been very impactful in helping us understand the quality of our product, what the gaps are and how to improve it. Stephen has also worked on the deployment and monitoring side of projects, including CI/CD pipelines and Devops style work of setting up and configuring models. He also built all our Python metrics dashboards to help us understand how the system is being used in production which has helped us spot issues users were having. Stephen is also a great communicator, he makes sure he understands the problem well, and ask thoughtful questions and always outlines a plan for how he is going to tackle a problem. He also moves fast, which is important in startups. On the personal side, I really enjoy working with Stephen. He has a lot of enthusiasm for building high quality AI systems, he is always very open, he is really good team player and is a great person. Overall, I would highly recommend Stephen, he would be a great asset to any company.

# *Meg-John Barker*, writer, mentor and associate at *Centre for Transforming Sexuality and Gender*, University of Brighton

I consider Stephen to be an exceptional researcher who would be an asset to any organisation. I have known Stephen for over a decade as a friend and colleague. I consider their work to be some of the most important and innovative in the field, and I frequently draw upon it in my own writing. We have also collaborated together on a number of projects. Most recently, I was a stakeholder/participant on their major funded project: ‘Mapping Mindfulness’. The ‘Mapping Mindfulness’ project employed an innovative participatory co-design, which meant that stakeholder/participants were engaged with in various ways throughout the research process. I certainly found that this approach enabled me to feel invested in the project, with the potential to engage in ways that ensured that the outcomes of the research would be helpful in relation to my own work. In all of their research, Stephen demonstrates clear, enthusiastic and insightful engagement with their stakeholders and participants, and a consistent commitment to ethical principles.
